evals.name: new-project-opencode-hook-scaffold
evals.prompt: I have a TypeScript monorepo with pnpm, Turborepo, `.envrc`, and no OpenCode plugin setup yet. Audit the repo first, verify the live official OpenCode plugin docs, inspect existing OpenCode config state, then scaffold a minimal project-local OpenCode lifecycle plugin that runs repo-owned validation after idle.
evals.expected_output: The response verifies live official OpenCode plugin sources first, audits the repo, chooses project-local scope, and creates one active TypeScript lifecycle/action plugin with a concise README and no broad surface catalog unless requested.

assertions.text: Response verifies the live official OpenCode plugin docs before scaffolding
Response inspects existing OpenCode config and plugin state before choosing scope
Response scaffolds `.opencode/plugins/`, not `.codex/hooks.json` or `.claude/settings.json`
Response generates one live lifecycle/action plugin and keeps project-specific work in repo-owned scripts
Generated lifecycle plugin resolves repo-owned scripts from the active OpenCode project/worktree/directory context
Response generates TypeScript `.ts` plugin files and no managed `.js` plugin files
Response avoids `.opencode/package.json`, lockfiles, and node_modules when no external plugin dependency is imported

evals.name: visible-lifecycle-follow-up
evals.prompt: Mirror my existing OpenCode session lifecycle automation. It should inject session context on session.created, run validation on session.idle, show visible OpenCode TUI feedback, and allow one automatic repair prompt without looping forever.
evals.expected_output: The response generates or updates a reusable lifecycle/action plugin that uses client.tui.showToast for visible start/pass/fail feedback, client.app.log for diagnostics, and client.session.prompt for one controlled repair pass followed by a noReply persistent-failure notice.

assertions.text: Generated plugin includes a best-effort showToast helper with info, success, warning, and error variants
Generated plugin keeps diagnostic logging separate from user-visible TUI feedback
Generated plugin tracks inFlight, repairPromptSent, and persistentFailureReported
Generated plugin sends only one automatic repair prompt and uses noReply for persistent failure

evals.name: existing-project-additive-refresh
evals.prompt: This repo already has `.opencode/plugins/` with a couple of hand-written plugins plus stale managed plugin state. Add the missing current hook surfaces, preserve the custom plugins, refresh only the managed plugin state and `hooks/opencode-*` adapters, and keep the managed README current.
evals.expected_output: The response chooses additive mode, preserves non-managed plugin files, refreshes the managed layer, and updates the managed README.

assertions.text: Response distinguishes managed plugin files from unrelated custom plugins
Response uses additive mode unless the managed layer is structurally stale

evals.name: scope-first-troubleshooting
evals.prompt: The repo already has `opencode.json` and `.opencode/plugins/`, but the plugin behavior is confusing. Before rewriting anything, inspect the current OpenCode config and plugin directories, determine whether the behavior is coming from project-local or global scope, and only then suggest changes.
evals.expected_output: The response treats config layering and plugin scope as the first diagnostic, inspects project and global state, and only then moves to code changes.

assertions.text: Response checks project-vs-global OpenCode setup before changing plugin files
Agent reads references/config-layering.md

evals.name: post-turn-lint-pattern
evals.prompt: Set up OpenCode so it runs my Biome or test check after the agent finishes editing files, but avoid thrashing the session. Use the official plugin docs first and then apply the post-turn pattern from the article carefully.
evals.expected_output: The response combines official plugin guidance with the secondary post-turn article, using `tool.execute.after` plus `event`/`session.idle` with edit tracking, visible TUI feedback, and a cooldown.

assertions.text: Response does not treat the article as authoritative over the official docs
Response uses edit tracking and cooldown for a post-turn validator
Response uses client.tui.showToast for meaningful background work instead of relying on client.app.log

evals.name: broad-surface-catalog-request
evals.prompt: Create a broad OpenCode plugin scaffold that shows me every currently known official hook surface as reference stubs, but keep only enabled plugins active at runtime.
evals.expected_output: The response uses the broad plan with surface_catalog enabled, writes non-loading managed surface stubs, and keeps active plugin modules separate from the reference catalog.

assertions.text: Response only generates the full hook-surface catalog because the user explicitly requested a broad scaffold
Response keeps dormant hook-surface examples outside the active plugin load path

evals.name: negative-codex-hooks-request
evals.prompt: I need Codex hooks scaffolded into `.codex/hooks.json` with `PreToolUse` and `Stop` handlers. Do that in this repo.
evals.expected_output: The response declines to use the OpenCode plugin scaffold and routes to the Codex-specific hook workflow instead.

assertions.text: Does not scaffold `.opencode/plugins/` for a Codex hook request
Does not hallucinate OpenCode plugin surfaces as Codex hook events
